title: Irrational Numbers and Their Locations on the Number Line

key_big: Irrational: the decimal never ends and never repeats.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • An irrational number cannot be written as a fraction of integers. Its decimal never ends and never repeats.
  • √2, √5, ∛10 and π are irrational. √49 = 7 and ∛8 = 2 are rational, because 49 and 8 are perfect powers.
  • To locate √30, find the perfect squares around it: 25 < 30 < 36, so 5 < √30 < 6, closer to 5.
  • π ≈ 3.14 is only an approximation.

Examples

Example

√40

36 < 40 < 49

6 < √40 < 7

Answer: about 6.3
